## Research

### Predicting In-Game Spending Behaviour Using Machine Learning (MSc thesis, 2026)

MSc Data Analytics for Business, Department of Data Analytics, Kedge Business School.
Supervised by Dr. Tianyuan Zhang.

- Question: which player behaviours and engagement patterns best predict in-game spending, and how can those predictors be interpreted through economic and behavioural theories of consumer choice?
- Data: five public datasets covering more than 50,000 players and 52,000 games (mobile, Steam and Roblox catalogues).
- Methods: interpretable logistic regression baseline, a thirteen-model classification benchmark, random forests, k-means segmentation, natural language processing, deep learning, Lorenz curves and Gini coefficients, cross-validation, class-imbalance handling.
- Finding: engagement and demographic features showed no robust association with spending — all thirteen classifiers performed at chance (ROC AUC 0.48–0.52) and no feature passed conventional significance tests. The structural patterns theory predicts were nonetheless clear: revenue Gini of 0.87, with the top 1% of payers generating 39% of revenue, and a playtime Gini of 0.83.
- Control: the same pipeline applied to two genuine game-level catalogues reached 0.95 ROC AUC and recovered the freemium signal from game descriptions alone via NLP.
- Interpretation: the behavioural signal is absent from synthetic and coarse public data rather than from the phenomenon itself, so credible prediction of individual spending requires real player-level telemetry — with direct implications for the ethics of behaviour-based monetisation.
- Thesis: https://www.zyadhusseini.com/research/Zyad-Husseini-MSc-Thesis-Predicting-In-Game-Spending.docx
- Proposal: https://www.zyadhusseini.com/research/Zyad-Husseini-MSc-Thesis-Proposal.pdf

### The Impact of Renewable Energy Adoption on Economic Growth (2025)

Econometrics research paper, Department of Economics, School of Business,
The American University in Cairo (ECON 408101, supervised by Dr. Mina Ayad).

- Question: do increases in renewable energy consumption spur economic growth?
- Data: World Bank World Development Indicators, 7 countries, 1990–2023, 238 country-year observations.
- Methods: panel OLS, White test, robust OLS, maximum likelihood estimation, fixed effects with year dummies, 2SLS instrumenting renewable consumption with its own lag, Cragg–Donald and underidentification tests, Newey–West, Hausman test, random effects.
- Finding: renewable energy consumption is consistently associated with slower short-run growth. Under 2SLS, a one-unit rise in the renewable share is associated with a 1.44 percentage point reduction in GDP per capita growth (p = 0.029). Gross capital formation is positive and highly significant; tertiary enrolment, trade openness and population growth are not significant in any specification.
- Interpretation: the result argues for sequencing the energy transition (efficiency, grid integration, workforce training, capital-formation incentives) rather than slowing decarbonisation.
- Paper: https://www.zyadhusseini.com/research/Zyad-Husseini-Renewable-Energy-Economic-Growth.pdf
- Stata do-file: https://www.zyadhusseini.com/research/renewable-energy-growth-stata.do
- Dataset: https://www.zyadhusseini.com/research/renewable-energy-growth-dataset.xlsx
